issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Implement version skew handling for in-place pod resize
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This is a tracking bug to implement two changes to better handle version skew as documented in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1287-in-place-update-pod-resources#version-skew-strategy
1. kubelet: When feature-gate is disabled, if kubelet sees a Proposed resize, it rejects the resize as Infeasible.
2. scheduler: If PodStatus.Resize field is not empty, scheduler uses max(ResourcesAllocated, Requests) even if the feature-gate is disabled.


### Why is this needed?

This is needed to gracefully handle component version skews that can occur during upgrades.

review_comments:
@vinaykul I wanted to ask you if it is really what we want?
I looked into the code once again and it seems suspicious for me.

We set `resize = infeasable` if the feature gate is disabled but we don't check if any resize is actually going on (sth like `!cmp.Equal(container.Resources.Requests, containerStatus.AllocatedResources)`). 

Maybe I'm missing sth, but I think we should add a check if the `Resources.Requests` is not equal to `AllocatedResources` indicating there is request for a change). 

Is it right?

I see your point, there are other cases to consider. For this issue, I want to focus on `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature gate is disabled on kubelet when it sees `PodStatus.Resize=Proposed` (i.e it was enabled on apiserver and a resize was requested).
The other key scenario that you are worried about is when user previously enabled InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature gate and resize is in-flight. Perhaps we can create a new issue for that if tests prove there is a problem? (There is already a bunch of ugly special code for container hash handling during the alpha/beta transition period. I just want to know how big of a problem it is and how much special code effort we want to invest into it that will get dropped once we go GA)

It would suffice to add an else block to this if fgEnabled where it sets s.Resize = Infeasible in case it is non-empty (Proposed should be the only value when feature is enabled on API and resize has been requested)

> in case it is non-empty

Could you clarify what should be non-empty here? `s`?
FYI I went with my gut feeling in the update, so you can validate if it is correct.
